notes.text: Did not we strictly command you, not to teach? — See the poor cunning of the enemies of the Gospel. They make laws and interdicts at their pleasure, which those who obey God cannot but break; and then take occasion thereby to censure and punish the innocent, as guilty. Ye would bring the blood of this man upon us - An artful and invidious word. The apostles did not desire to accuse any man. They simply declared the naked truth.

Then Peter — In the name of all the apostles, said - He does not now give them the titles of honour, which he did before, chap. iv, 8; but enters directly upon the subject, and justifies what he had done. This is, as it were, a continuation of that discourse, but with an increase of severity.
Hath raised up Jesus — Of the seed of David, according to the promises made to our fathers.

Him hath God exalted — From the grave to heaven; to give repentance - Whereby Jesus is received as a Prince; and forgiveness of sins - Whereby he is received as a saviour. Hence some infer, that repentance and faith are as mere gifts as remission of sins. Not so: for man co-operates in the former, but not in the latter. God alone forgives sins.
And also the Holy Ghost — A much greater witness.

glossa.text:
*By commanding* etc. In the Greek: *Did we not by commanding command you?* For to speak thus better befits one who questions. *You have filled Jerusalem.* The chief of cities, in which we also dwell. In this they praise the apostles unwittingly, who, terrified by threats, cease not to preach. *Upon us the blood. ((RAB.))* It is plain that it was said by antiphrasis: *His blood be upon us.*

The rash questioning of the high priest is refuted by a prudent answer.

((ID.)) They question, for there is wont to be doubt in words, when in the heart a fixed opinion is held.
*The God of the fathers. ((RAB.))* Not new, nor lately found out by us: but he says this, that their disobedience may be inexcusable.

*The Holy Spirit.* The Holy Spirit has strengthened us, that even though you resist we may firmly preach the great works of God, speaking in us and forming the words which you hear.

*To all. ((RAB.))* Not to us alone, but to all that obey, to you also, if you will receive. In this he calls them to penance.

notes.text: Salvation — My saviour.
Doth valiantly — These are the words of that song of praise now mentioned.
Exalted — Hath appeared evidently, and wrought powerfully and gloriously.
Open — O ye porters, appointed by God for this work. The gates - Of the Lord's tabernacle: where the rule of righteousness was kept and taught, and the sacrifices of righteousness were offered.

The righteous — As David was a type of Christ and the temple of heaven, so this place hath a farther prospect than David, and relates to Christ's ascending into heaven, and opening the gates of that blessed temple, both for himself and for all believers.

The builders — The commonwealth of Israel and the church of God are here and elsewhere compared to a building, wherein, as the people are the stones, so the princes and rulers are the builders. And as these master-builders rejected David, so their successors rejected Christ. Head stone - The chief stone in the whole building, by which the several parts of the building are upheld and firmly united together. Thus David united all the tribes and families of Israel: and thus Christ united Jews and Gentiles together. And therefore this place is justly expounded of Christ, Mark xii, 10 Acts iv, 11 Rom. ix, 32 Eph. ii, 20. And to him the words agree more properly than to David.
Made — Or sanctified as a season never to be forgotten.
We — These seem to be the words of the Levites, to whom he spake ver. 19.

Blessed — We pray that God would bless his person and government. Cometh - To the throne; or from his Father into the world: who is known by the name of him that cometh or was to come, and of whom this very word is used, Gen. xlix, 10 Isaiah xxxv, 4. Name - By commission from him. We - We who are the Lord's ministers attending upon him in his house, and appointed to bless in his name, Num. vi, 23 Deut. x, 8. So these are the words of the priests.

The Lord — Or, The mighty God, as this name of God signifies, and as he shewed himself to be by this, his wonderful work. Who - Who hath scattered our dark clouds, and put us into a state of peace, and safety, and happiness. The horns - These are supposed to be made for this very use, that the beasts should be bound and killed there. These three last verses are David's words. Because this psalm was very large, and the matter of it of the greatest importance, the psalmist thought fit to divide it into two and twenty several parts, according to the number of the Hebrew letters, that he might both prevent tediousness, and fix it in the memory. Each part consists of eight verses. All the verses of the first part beginning with Aleph, all the verses of the second with Beth, and so on. It is observable, that the word of God is here called by the names of law, statutes, precepts or commandments, judgments, ordinances, righteousness, testimonies, way and word. By which variety, he designed to express the nature and perfection of God's word. It is called his word, as revealed by him to us; his way, as prescribed by him for us to walk in; his law, as binding us to obedience; his statutes, as declaring his authority of giving us laws; his precepts as directing our duty; his ordinances, as ordained by him; his righteousness, as exactly agreeable to God's righteous nature and will; his judgments, as proceeding from the great judge of the world, and being his judicial sentence to which all men must submit; and his testimonies, as it contains the witness of God's will, and of man's duty. And there is but one of these one hundred and seventy six verses, in which one or other of these titles is not found. The general scope and design of this psalm is, to magnify the law and make it honourable: to shew the excellency and usefulness of divine Revelation, and recommend it to us, by the psalmist's own example, who speaks by experience of the benefits of it, for which he praises God, and earnestly prays for the continuance of God's grace, to direct and quicken him in his way.

glossa.text: *He is become my salvation.* ((ID.)) He is not made what he was not to himself; but he is salvation to them converted, which he was not to them turned away.
*I shall not die.* ((ID.)) The Church says it, since the persecutor thinks that by a slaughter of funerals he can blot out the Christian name, whereas he rather increases it.

*Chastising.* ((CASS.)) But why he bore so many things, he shows: *Chastising,* whatever they do is the chastisement of the Lord. Let them claim nothing to themselves; he is not given over to death whose vices are purged. ((AUG.)) Often a father amends his sons by worthless servants, when for those he prepares punishment, for these an inheritance. And what the inheritance is may be known from this: *Open ye the gates.* What within? *Having entered I will confess.*

*Open ye.* ((CASS.)) In the third place he desires that the gates of Jerusalem be opened to him, where he speaks also of the corner stone. Open, O prophets, who bear the keys of the kingdom of heaven. *The gates.* ((CASS., HIER.)) They who have entered through these gates of doctrine praise truly; outside the Catholic Church there is no praise of God. ((CASS.)) All these gates lead to one, which is Christ, through whom the just enter into heaven; whence: *I am the door, through which if any man enter in, he shall be safe ((Joan. X))* . And elsewhere: *No man cometh to the Father, but by me ((Joan. XIV))*. ((AUG.)) Behold, he has made mention of both worlds: and because this gate has appeared as Christ, *I will confess to thee,* giving thanks with gladness, *because thou hast heard* at the coming of the Son; for the just of former times were asking for the coming. *The gates of justice.* That is, the gates of death, etc., *as far as* that is, through it unto life.
*They that build.* ((ID.)) The Jews alone, worshipping God, were building, the rest being destroyed through idolatry; but they did not finish, because they despised Christ.
*This is done by the Lord.* Or, *This is done by the Lord for him,* according to another reading. ((ID.)) That is, unto the honour of the Father.

*This is the day.* This is the jubilee year, figuratively observed under the law, which is called *remitting,* or *beginning,* because then bondmen were set free, possessions were restored to their owners: and we on this day have been redeemed from the servitude of sin, to whom an eternal inheritance has been restored. ((CASS.)) *This is the day.* Although he made all days, this one singularly, on which the Lord came, on which it is fitting to rejoice, because the devil lost his right and man lived again; and because this is so,
*O Lord, save,* etc. Behold the desire of a great petition. *Save,* from the ruin of the world. *Give prosperity,* that these sorrows may be turned into eternal joys.

*Blessed,* etc. ((CASS.)) Fourthly he urges that the courts of God be frequented, rejoicing in the coming of Christ. ((AUG.)) Cursed therefore is he that comes in his own name, etc., *as far as* he who shall be cursed. ((CASS.)) *Blessed.* Praise for the coming; and, O ye other Christians, we the elders, as it were priests, *have blessed you,* which profits much, because *we have blessed you out of the house of the Lord.*

*Out of the house.* ((ID.)) That is, the Catholic Church, etc., *as far as* because glad is the confession that follows benefits.

*Appoint a day.* ((AUG.)) The great, who go beyond, who with the mind touch the Word, God with God, etc., *as far as* that is, that he may attain unto eternal joys.

 *A solemn day.* In the old law ((Deut. X.)) the Pasch, Pentecost, the feast of tabernacles, three chief solemnities, in which it was commanded that no man should appear empty in the sight of the Lord. He is empty who has not Christ in himself, who is the foundation, which no man is able to change. Hence it is that on those three solemnities the faithful people offers a coin by an offering of the hand, signifying the inward offering. For on a coin there is the name and image of the king. Let each one therefore offer a coin spiritually, that he may have in himself the *name* of the king, that is, of Christ, being called a Christian from Christ; and may show forth to God the *image,* that is, the soul, marked with the light of his countenance. *The horn of the altar.* ((CASS.)) Or by the *altar* is understood the sacrament of the body and blood, etc., *as far as he shall not have life everlasting.*

Or, the *altar* is understood to be the mind of man; whence in the law it was commanded ((Exod. XXVII)) that an altar be made four-cornered and hollow: four-cornered, because the human mind ought to be fortified with four virtues, prudence, justice, fortitude, temperance; and the same ought to be hollow to receive the word of God and the fire of love. For swelling drives back what is poured in; whence in Leviticus it is commanded ((Levit. I)) that the little bladder of the throat and the feathers be cast away, when a turtle-dove or a pigeon is offered. The bladder signifies the puffing up of pride; the feathers, empty searchings into lofty things; cast these away therefore, that thou mayest be a hollow altar.

*Thou art my God.* And that we may speak more openly, this is the sense of these words: Let not this feast day upon earth, on which the lamb was slain, suffice: but let it be appointed in frequent celebrations, until with minds exalted we come to his inward Godhead, where we shall sing praises thus: *Thou art my God,* etc. And so, as he began with praise, so he ends with it.
*Give praise to the Lord.* From the beginning which we forsook, unto the end to which we return, there is nothing more wholesome, which may delight, than the praise of God

notes.text: John — The dedication of this book is contained in the fourth, fifth, and sixth verses; but the whole Revelation is a kind of letter. To the seven churches which are in Asia - That part of the Lesser Asia which was then a Roman province. There had been several other churches planted here; but it seems these were now the most eminent; and it was among these that St. John had laboured most during his abode in Asia. In these cities there were many Jews. Such of them as believed in each were joined with the gentile believers in one church. Grace be unto you, and peace - The favour of God, with all temporal and eternal blessings. From him who is, and who was, and who cometh, or, who is to come - A wonderful translation of the great name JEHOVAH: he was of old, he is now, he cometh; that is, will be forever. And from the seven spirits which are before his throne - Christ is he who "hath the seven spirits of God." "The seven lamps which burn before the throne are the seven spirits of God." " The lamb hath seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God." Seven was a sacred number in the Jewish church: but it did not always imply a precise number. It sometimes is to be taken figuratively, to denote completeness or perfection. By these seven spirits, not seven created angels, but the Holy Ghost is to be understood. The angels are never termed spirits in this book; and when all the angels stand up, while the four living creatures and the four and twenty elders worship him that sitteth on the throne, and the Lamb, the seven spirits neither stand up nor worship. To these "seven spirits of God," the seven churches, to whom the Spirit speaks so many things, are subordinate; as are also their angels, yea, and "the seven angels which stand before God." He is called the seven spirits, not with regard to his essence, which is one, but with regard to his manifold operations.

And from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the first begotten from the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth — Three glorious appellations are here given him, and in their proper order. He was the faithful witness of the whole will of God before his death, and in death, and remains such in glory. He rose from the dead, as "the first fruits of them that slept;" and now hath all power both in heaven and earth. He is here styled a prince: but by and by he hears his title of king; yea, King of kings, and Lord of lords." This phrase, the kings of the earth, signifies their power and multitude, and also the nature of their kingdom. It became the Divine Majesty to call them kings with a limitation; especially in this manifesto from his heavenly kingdom; for no creature, much less a sinful man, can bear the title of king in an absolute sense before the eyes of God.

To him that loveth us, and, out of that free, abundant love, hath washed us from the guilt and power of our sins with his own blood, and hath made us kings — Partakers of his present, and heirs of his eternal, kingdom. And priests unto his God and Father - To whom we continually offer ourselves, an holy, living sacrifice. To him be the glory - For his love and redemption. And the might - Whereby he governs all things.

Behold — In this and the next verse is the proposition, and the summary of the whole book. He cometh - Jesus Christ. Throughout this book, whenever it is said, He cometh, it means his glorious coming. The preparation for this began at the destruction of Jerusalem, and more particularly at the time of writing this book; and goes on, without any interruption, till that grand event is accomplished. Therefore it is never said in this book, He will come; but, He cometh. And yet it is not said, He cometh again: for when he came before, it was not like himself, but in "the form of a servant." But his appearing in glory is properly his coming; namely, in a manner worthy of the Son of God. And every eye - Of the Jews in particular. Shall see him - But with what different emotions, according as they had received or rejected him. And they who have pierced him - They, above all, who pierced his hands, or feet, or side. Thomas saw the print of these wounds even after his resurrection; and the same, undoubtedly, will be seen by all, when he cometh in the clouds of heaven. And all the tribes of the earth - The word tribes, in the Revelation, always means the Israelites: but where another word, such as nations or people, is joined with it, it implies likewise (as here) all the rest of mankind. Shall wail because of him - For terror and pain, if they did not wail before by true repentance. Yea, Amen - This refers to, every eye shall see him. He that cometh saith, Yea; he that testifies it, Amen. The word translated yea is Greek; Amen is Hebrew: for what is here spoken respects both Jew and gentile.

I am the Alpha and the Omega, saith the Lord God — Alpha is the first, Omega, the last, letter in the Greek alphabet. Let his enemies boast and rage ever so much in the intermediate time, yet the Lord God is both the Alpha, or beginning, and the Omega, or end, of all things. God is the beginning, as he is the Author and Creator of all things, and as he proposes, declares, and promises so great things: he is the end, as he brings all the things which are here revealed to a complete and glorious conclusion. Again, the beginning and end of a thing is in scripture styled the whole thing. Therefore God is the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end; that is, one who is all things, and always the same.

glossa.text: *To the seven churches.* He writes principally to those churches of Asia over which he had been set as master, and by likeness to the others. God gave to Christ, Christ to John, but John to the churches, or, through the seven, to the universal Church. Because *seven* signify universality, or because they are enlightened by the sevenfold Spirit. *In Asia.* Asia is a lifting up, the Church therefore is now in a lifting up of virtues, or once of vices. This Asia is not that great third part of the world, but a certain province where there were seven cities, and seven churches with seven bishops. *Grace be unto you.* He prepares his hearers in the salutation, and renders them well-disposed and attentive, as also in the prologue. *Who is and who was.* Eternally. But although he was born in time, he who once had been corruptible is now unchangeable through his humanity. Such is he to come, even if he does not appear such to the world. *And from the seven spirits, who in the sight. Spirit.* It sounds the same as charity. Whence to the Spirit is attributed the remission of sins, and the other gifts which are gifts of the whole Trinity, that we may understand the Trinity to work out of love alone. He is silent of the person of the Father, because concerning God the Creator no one had understood evil things, he sets down the person of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, concerning whom all heresies are born in the churches. *Thrones.* The thrones of God are his angels and holy men, in whom God now sits and judges, lest in time to come he judge.

*The faithful witness.* He says this because of those who despair of the death of Christ, as those who said: *We thought that it was he that should have redeemed Israel ((Luc. XXIV))*. *The firstborn of the dead.* As if he should say: Let it not terrify you, because he rose again, and is impassible. Or he is the first of those who mortify themselves, because he did no sin. *The prince of the kings of the earth.* The prince of the earthly powers, able to remove them, and, for the profit of his own or of the saints, permitting the ungodly to serve.
*And hath made us a kingdom to our God.* That is, powerful to resist vices, *and priests,* that is, offering our own selves to God for ourselves and for our brethren.

*Behold he cometh,* etc. And truly you ought to glorify him, because it is he who is to come to reward. *With the clouds,* that is, with the saints: because they were clouds in raining down doctrine upon others, and in working miracles; or, as he ascended in a cloud, so in a cloud will he come, by which we understand the clemency of God, whereby to the good there is refreshment and illumination, but to the evil terror and blinding. Which was also signified by the cloud whereby the children of Israel were led out of Egypt.

*And shall see him.* Another translation has: *All the earth shall see such a one.* As if he should say: Such shall they see him as the ungodly did not believe he would come. *Every eye.* The good shall see that they may rejoice, the evil that they may be confounded. *They shall bewail.* Or they shall dash themselves together over him, powerless to resist his command, after the likeness of a stone and of earthen vessels. Or *they shall bewail themselves,* that is, they shall grieve, looking back upon those who are founded upon him, because they shall not grieve so much over the torment itself, as that they shall be driven back from such fellowship.

*I am.* Truly he will come, because he himself promises that he will come. Or, the salutation being set first, he renders them attentive, as if he should say: Believe not this to have been said by me, but by Christ himself. *Alpha, the beginning.* Before whom is none, or from whom all things began. *Omega, the end.* After whom is none, or in whom all things shall be ended.

notes.text: Mark xvi, 14 Luke xxiv, 36.

Peace be unto you — This is the foundation of the mission of a true Gospel minister, peace in his own soul, 2 Cor. iv, 1. As the Father hath sent me, so send I you - Christ was the apostle of the Father, Heb. iii, 1. Peter and the rest, the apostles of Christ.

He breathed on them — New life and vigour, and saith, as ye receive this breath out of my mouth, so receive ye the Spirit out of my fulness: the Holy Ghost influencing you in a peculiar manner, to fit you for your great embassy. This was an earnest of pentecost.

Whosoever sins ye remit — (According to the tenor of the Gospel, that is, supposing them to repent and believe) they are remitted, and whosoever sins ye retain (supposing them to remain impenitent) they are retained. So far is plain. But here arises a difficulty. Are not the sins of one who truly repents, and unfeignedly believes in Christ, remitted, without sacerdotal absolution? And are not the sins of one who does not repent or believe, retained even with it? What then does this commission imply? Can it imply any more than,

1. A power of declaring with authority the Christian terms of pardon; whose sins are remitted and whose retained? As in our daily form of absolution; and

2. A power of inflicting and remitting ecclesiastical censures? That is, of excluding from, and re-admitting into, a Christian congregation.
After eight days — On the next Sunday.

And Thomas said, My Lord and my God — The disciples had said, We have seen the Lord. Thomas now not only acknowledges him to be the Lord, as he had done before, and to be risen, as his fellow disciples had affirmed, but also confesses his Godhead, and that more explicitly than any other had yet done. And all this he did without putting his hand upon his side.
Jesus wrought many miracles, which are not written in this book — Of St. John, nor indeed of the other evangelists.
But these things are written that ye may believe — That ye may be confirmed in believing. Faith cometh sometimes by reading; though ordinarily by hearing.

glossa.text: *When therefore,* etc. This was done on the very day of the resurrection, on which Jesus appeared five times. First to Mary Magdalene, secondly to the same woman running with the others who wished to announce it to the disciples, thirdly to Peter, fourthly to Cleophas and his companion, fifthly to the disciples, the doors being shut, the two aforesaid having now returned.

*He shewed them his hands and his side.* After the resurrection the Lord showed in his body two contrary things: both what was palpable, of the same nature, that he might form them to faith, and what was incorruptible, of another glory, that he might invite them to the reward.

*He said therefore to them again. Peace be to you,* etc. He offers peace, who came for the sake of peace; he repeats it, that he may show that through his blood the things that are in heaven and the things that are on earth have been made peaceful.
*Receive ye the Holy Ghost. ((AUG.))* On earth the spirit is given that the neighbour may be loved; from heaven the Spirit is given that God may be loved.

*Whose sins you shall forgive.* Behold charity, which is poured into their hearts through the Holy Ghost. He forgives the sins of those who are partakers of him; of those who are not, he retains them. And therefore after he had said: *Receive ye the Holy Ghost,* he immediately subjoined: *Whose sins you shall forgive.*

*Now Thomas, one.* Not by chance, but by divine disposition was Thomas absent, and he did not believe what he heard; whence the Lord offered himself to him to be handled, because by his doubting, and by the proof made to him, it is now left to no one to doubt. *Who is called Didymus.* Didymus, that is, twin, because Thomas is doubtful; that is, an abyss: because by doubting he knew more deeply.
*He answered.* He was seeing and touching the man, and above this he believed him God, doubt being now removed, and he confessed him whom he did not see.

*Because thou hast seen me, Thomas, thou hast believed.* He does not say, thou hast touched, but, thou hast seen: because sight is in a manner the general sense, which is wont to be said of the other four. Perhaps he did not dare to touch; but by looking only, or even by touching, he believes.

*Blessed.* He commends the faith of the Gentiles, but he uses the past tense, as one who knew that what was to come was already done in his own predestination.

echoes.text: If a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he is put to death, and you hang him on a tree; his body shall not remain all night on the tree, but you shall surely bury him the same day; for he who is hanged is accursed of God; that you don’t defile your land which Yahweh your God gives you for an inheritance.
echoes.note: 'Hanging him on a tree' (v. 30) draws directly on the law that a man executed and hung 'on a tree' is under God's curse. Acts deliberately uses xylon ('tree/wood'), the LXX term, to characterize the crucifixion in the categories of this statute. High volume and clear verbal dependence.

echoes.text: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered the king, Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you in this matter. If it happens, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace; and he will deliver us out of your hand, O king. But if not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods, nor worship the golden image which you have set up.
echoes.note: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse the king's command to disobey God, declaring they will serve God whatever the cost — the paradigm for 'We must obey God rather than men' (v. 29).

echoes.text: When Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem) and he kneeled on his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did before.
echoes.note: Daniel defies the royal decree to continue worshiping God, modeling principled obedience to God over human authority, the stance Peter articulates in v. 29.

echoes.text: God said moreover to Moses, “You shall tell the children of Israel this, ‘Yahweh, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is my name forever, and this is my memorial to all generations.
echoes.note: 'The God of our fathers' (v. 30) is the self-designation revealed to Moses at the bush, anchoring the apostolic proclamation in the covenant identity of Israel's God.

echoes.text: The right hand of Yahweh is exalted! The right hand of Yahweh does valiantly!”
echoes.note: 'The right hand of the LORD is exalted' lies behind 'God exalted him with his right hand' (v. 31); Psalm 118 is a primary early-church resource for the vindication of the rejected one.

echoes.text: Yahweh says to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool for your feet.”
echoes.note: The enthronement 'at the right hand' of God underwrites the exaltation of Jesus 'with his right hand' as Prince and Savior (v. 31), the dominant NT proof-text for the session.

echoes.text: Afterward Joshua struck them, put them to death, and hanged them on five trees. They were hanging on the trees until the evening.
echoes.note: The execution of enemy kings by hanging on trees illustrates the legal practice behind Deut 21 invoked in v. 30; a secondary witness to 'hanging on a tree.'

echoes.text: let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts; and let him return to Yahweh, and he will have mercy on him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.
echoes.note: The call to return for abundant pardon stands faintly behind 'to give repentance to Israel and remission of sins' (v. 31).

echoes.text: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM,” and he said, “You shall tell the children of Israel this: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
echoes.note: 'Who is and who was and who is to come' expands the divine Name of Exod 3:14 (LXX ho ōn, 'the one who is') into a three-tense formula. High thematic coherence on the eternal self-existent God; John adds 'who was' and 'who is to come' to render the Tetragrammaton's timelessness, a known Targumic/Hellenistic-Jewish expansion.

echoes.text: and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel.”
echoes.note: 'He made us to be a Kingdom, priests to his God' directly reapplies the Sinai covenant charter 'a kingdom of priests' to the church. Strong verbal volume; John follows a reading like 'kingdom and priests' (cf. LXX basileion hierateuma), democratizing Israel's vocation onto the redeemed.

echoes.text: I will also appoint him my firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
echoes.note: 'The firstborn of the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth' fuses both halves of Ps 89:27 (LXX 88:28), the royal-messianic enthronement of David's heir. Two distinct phrases recur together (firstborn + highest/ruler of earth's kings), giving high verbal volume; Christ's resurrection becomes the 'firstborn' coronation.

echoes.text: Behold, I have given him for a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander to the peoples.
echoes.note: 'The faithful witness' coheres with Isaiah's messianic 'witness to the peoples.' Thematic and partial verbal overlap on the title 'witness'; less distinctive than the Ps 89 / Exod echoes, so medium and arguably secondary.

echoes.text: Then he answered and spoke to me, saying, “This is Yahweh’s word to Zerubbabel, saying, ‘Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit,’ says Yahweh of Armies.
echoes.note: The 'seven Spirits before his throne' may draw on Zechariah's vision-cycle of the Spirit and the seven lamps/eyes (Zech 4:2, 10). Faint; the sevenfold Spirit more likely develops Isa 11:2's enumerated Spirit, so low confidence and contested.

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
echoes.note: 'He is coming with the clouds' lifts Daniel's 'one like a son of man' coming 'with the clouds of the sky.' Very high verbal volume and recurrence (this is Revelation's signature christophany text); John applies Daniel's heavenward enthronement to Christ's parousia toward earth.

echoes.text: I will pour on the house of David, and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplication; and they will look to me whom they have pierced; and they shall mourn for him, as one mourns for his only son, and will grieve bitterly for him, as one grieves for his firstborn.
echoes.note: 'Those who pierced him' and 'all the tribes will mourn' weave together Zech 12:10's piercing and mourning. High verbal volume; John follows the Hebrew 'whom they pierced' (the LXX reads 'because they mocked/danced'), agreeing with John 19:37 against the LXX — a noted Hebrew-vs-LXX divergence.
echoes.lxxText: And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and compassion: and they shall look upon me, because they have mocked me, and they shall make lamentation for him, as for a beloved friend, and they shall grieve intensely, as for a firstborn son.

echoes.text: The land will mourn, every family apart; the family of the house of David apart, and their wives apart; the family of the house of Nathan apart, and their wives apart;
echoes.note: 'All the tribes of the earth will mourn over him' extends Zech 12:12's catalog of mourning families. Reinforces the Zechariah piercing-and-mourning complex; John universalizes Zechariah's tribes of the land into 'all the tribes of the earth.'

echoes.text: This is what Yahweh, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Yahweh of Armies, says: “I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God.
echoes.note: 'I am the Alpha and the Omega' is a Greek-alphabet equivalent of Isaiah's divine self-predication 'I am the first and the last.' High thematic coherence with the Deutero-Isaianic monotheism formula; John recasts the merism into the first and last Greek letters, claiming exhaustive divine sovereignty.

echoes.text: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM,” and he said, “You shall tell the children of Israel this: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
echoes.note: The repeated 'who is and who was and who is to come' restates the Exod 3:14 Name (LXX ho ōn). Recurrence from 1:4 raises verbal volume; here joined to 'the Almighty' (LXX pantokratōr), the standard rendering of 'Yahweh of Armies / El Shaddai.'

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
echoes.note: Jesus 'breathed on them' and said 'Receive the Holy Spirit' — the verb (enephysesen, LXX of Gen 2:7) directly evokes God breathing the breath of life into Adam's nostrils so he became a living being. John presents the Spirit-impartation as new creation/new Adam; very high Volume given the rare shared verb and high Coherence with the Gospel's creation theology.

echoes.text: Then he said to me, Prophesy to the wind, prophesy, son of man, and tell the wind, Thus says the Lord Yahweh: Come from the four winds, breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live. So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up on their feet, an exceedingly great army.
echoes.note: 'Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live' stands behind Jesus breathing Spirit into the disciples after the resurrection. Ezekiel's vivified corpses give the scene its resurrection-and-Spirit valence; high Coherence and shared breath/Spirit (ruach/pneuma) vocabulary reinforce the Genesis 2:7 figure.

echoes.text: ‘Yahweh bless you, and keep you. Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
echoes.note: The risen Jesus' threefold greeting 'Peace be to you' (20:19,21,26) functions as the eschatological enactment of the Aaronic priestly blessing 'the LORD lift up his countenance on you and give you peace.' Medium Volume (shared 'peace') with strong Coherence as the resurrected high-priestly Lord blesses his gathered people.

echoes.text: I will lay the key of the house of David on his shoulder. He will open, and no one will shut. He will shut, and no one will open.
echoes.note: The authority to forgive or retain sins ('he shall open, and no one shall shut; he shall shut, and no one shall open') parallels the key-of-the-house-of-David grant of binding/loosing power. The remit-or-retain antithesis matches the open/shut structure of the oracle; medium confidence on the structural rather than verbal link.

echoes.text: Because he was ignorant of him that moulded him, And of him that inspired into him an active soul, And breathed into him a vital spirit.
echoes.note: 'He failed to know the one who formed him and inspired him with an active soul and breathed into him a living spirit' restates Gen 2:7 in Second-Temple idiom, evidencing the availability of the breath-of-life motif John reworks. Deuterocanonical witness rather than a direct source.

echoes.text: I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake; and I will not remember your sins.
echoes.note: 'I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake' grounds the forgiveness of sins as a divine prerogative now delegated to the disciples (20:23). Faint background highlighting that sin-forgiveness is God's act, sharpening the Christological claim.

echoes.text: Wake up! Rise up to defend me, my God! My Lord, contend for me!
echoes.note: Thomas' confession 'My Lord and my God!' (20:28) reproduces the psalmist's vocative 'my God and my Lord' (LXX Ps 34:23: ho theos mou kai ho kyrios mou). The unusual paired address gives high Volume; John climaxes the Gospel by directing to Jesus the cry the psalmist directs to YHWH.

echoes.text: But you, Lord, are a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth.
echoes.note: Thomas addresses Jesus with the divine titles 'Lord... God' that the psalter repeatedly couples ('you, O Lord, are a God merciful and gracious'), reinforcing the deliberate transfer of YHWH-language to the risen Christ. Supporting Recurrence behind the primary Ps 35:23 allusion.

echoes.text: Behold, his soul is puffed up. It is not upright in him, but the righteous will live by his faith.
echoes.note: 'Blessed are those who have not seen, and have believed' (20:29) coheres with 'the righteous shall live by his faith,' the OT charter of faith-not-sight. Thematic rather than verbal; faint and one of several wisdom/faith backgrounds.

echoes.text: Yahweh answered me, “Write the vision, and make it plain on tablets, that he who runs may read it. For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
echoes.note: 'These are written, that you may believe' enacts the prophetic command 'Write the vision; make it plain... it awaits its appointed time,' grounding the inscribed witness-for-faith in the OT theology of the written vision that calls for belief. Medium Coherence with the Gospel's purpose statement; verbal contact is on the writing-for-faith motif.

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book. Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. Those who are wise shall […]
echoes.note: The notion of words 'written in this book' so that the faithful 'may have life' faintly recalls Daniel's sealed book and those 'found written in the book' who awake to everlasting life. Low Volume; offered as a faint life-through-the-book resonance.

echoes.text: I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
echoes.note: The confessional goal 'that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God' draws on the royal-messianic decree 'You are my Son,' the OT title-cluster (Messiah / Son of God) John affirms. Background to the titulature rather than a quotation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Christ is risen!
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
The doors were locked, and fear was in the room,
and Jesus came and stood among them: Peace be with you.
He showed his wounded hands; he breathed on them the Spirit.
My Lord and my God!
Blessed are those who have not seen and yet believe.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Come into the locked room where the doors are shut and the fear sits heavy as evening.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Into that closed and frightened place he comes and stands, and the first word out of his mouth is peace.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
He holds out his hands, still marked, still wounded, and says: reach here, touch, and do not doubt.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
He breathes on them — the same breath that moved over the waters — and says: receive the Holy Spirit.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
So bring your locked rooms and your honest doubts, and hear him speak peace again:
Christ is risen, Alleluia!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The doors are locked; the room is full of fear.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
He comes and stands among us: Peace be with you.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
He shows his wounded hands and breathes out the Spirit.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
My Lord and my God — come, let us worship.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
